entry.title: Could this potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments? #TEDTalks

media:group.media:title: Could this potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments? #TEDTalks
media:group.media:description: What if medicines could "speak" directly to your cells? Protein designer and TED Fellow Chris Bahl introduces a new generation of miniproteins: AI-designed medicines that can deliver detailed instructions to fix what's making you sick. He shares how this breakthrough could potentially unlock safer, more effective treatments for some of humanity's most challenging diseases.

entry.title: Why Great Art Requires Risk | Alex Van Halen, David Lee Roth and Robert Vargas | TED

media:group.media:title: Why Great Art Requires Risk | Alex Van Halen, David Lee Roth and Robert Vargas | TED
media:group.media:description:
Van Halen drummer and co-founder Alex Van Halen and lead singer David Lee Roth sit down with visual artist Robert Vargas, who paints freehand murals up to twenty stories tall, to reveal the two-step recipe behind great art: do your homework, then break every rule. Along the way, they swap stories about heartbreak, good luck charms — and why you should rehearse for what goes wrong. (Recorded at TEDxFargo on July 29, 2026)

entry.title: Want Someone to Change? Ask This Question | Philip Jameson | TED

media:group.media:title: Want Someone to Change? Ask This Question | Philip Jameson | TED
media:group.media:description:
Why is it so hard to get someone to change? Leadership expert Philip Jameson has spent years watching people pitch smart ideas at work, only to be met with colleagues resistant to adjusting how things get done. He breaks down why people push back against change — and the one question that could help your next idea take flight. (Recorded at TED@BCG on August 18, 2026)

entry.title: Why Clean Energy Is an Unstoppable Force | Michael Liebreich | TED

media:group.media:title: Why Clean Energy Is an Unstoppable Force | Michael Liebreich | TED
media:group.media:description:
Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing? Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again. Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required. The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected. (Recorded at TED Countdown: The Next Ten on October 15, 2026)

entry.title: "Deep listening” can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and divides #TEDTalks

media:group.media:title: "Deep listening” can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and divides #TEDTalks
media:group.media:description: Do you avoid talking to people you disagree with? Author and mediator Emily Kasriel thinks you should try it out. She explains why engaging with ideas that bother you is one of the most powerful things you can do — and presents her framework for “deep listening” that can help you form relationships across generations, cultures and political divides.

entry.title: The harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way #TEDTalks

media:group.media:title: The harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way #TEDTalks
media:group.media:description: When life gets uncertain, do you grip a little tighter? Neuroscientist Heather Berlin explores a surprising paradox: the harder you try to control everything, the more likely you are to get in your own way. Drawing on brain research and her own struggles with uncertainty, she shares practical ways to let go and make room for creativity, calm and flow.

entry.title: How to Teach a Robot to Dance | David Dobáš | TED

media:group.media:title: How to Teach a Robot to Dance | David Dobáš | TED
media:group.media:description:
Teaching a robot to dance, move or even stand up used to take countless hours of training. Now, by simply recording a video, you can teach a robot a new skill in a fraction of the time, says roboticist David Dobáš. In a live demo with TED guest curator Bilawal Sidhu, Dobáš shows how advances in AI are transforming the way these humanoid machines learn — and proves it with a robot dance performance at the end.(Recorded at David Dobáš on April 17, 2026)

entry.title: Making the vaccine was never the hardest part— it was getting people to trust them #TEDTalks

media:group.media:title: Making the vaccine was never the hardest part— it was getting people to trust them #TEDTalks
media:group.media:description: What good is a vaccine people don't trust? Immunologist and TED Fellow Kizzmekia Corbett co-developed the first COVID-19 vaccine to enter clinical trials — but she says making the vaccine was never the hardest part. The real obstacle is the gap between scientists and the people who have honest questions about the shots they're being asked to take. She shares a refreshing approach for taking on vaccine inquisitiveness and ensuring that humanity is ready for the next pandemic.

entry.title: The Science of Learning New Things | Tania Lombrozo | TED

media:group.media:title: The Science of Learning New Things | Tania Lombrozo | TED
media:group.media:description:
With more information at our fingertips than ever before, learning should be getting easier ... yet the opposite seems to be true, says cognitive scientist Tania Lombrozo. Drawing on her research into how our minds understand and reason, she explores why more information can actually make learning harder — and shares the critical skill all great learners possess. (Recorded at TEDxNewEngland on October 30, 2025)

entry.title: What People Living in Democracies Take for Granted | Leopoldo López | TED

media:group.media:title: What People Living in Democracies Take for Granted | Leopoldo López | TED
media:group.media:description:
Activist Leopoldo López learned the true value of freedom in a solitary confinement cell, when someone else decided if he would eat or see sunlight. In this searching conversation, he explains why democracy is losing ground across the globe, the state of Venezuela's transition after Maduro's capture and the 2026 earthquakes — and why he founded the World Liberty Congress to unite activists in the fight against autocracies. (This conversation, hosted by TED's Whitney Pennington Rogers, was part of an exclusive TED Membership event. entry.title: How Would You Design Your Dream City? | James Rojas | TED

media:group.media:title: How Would You Design Your Dream City? | James Rojas | TED
media:group.media:description:
Urban planner James Rojas has led hundreds of workshops where participants creatively design their ideal communities with small objects — and he's noticed that people of every age, income and background build strikingly similar places. Through play and storytelling, he shows how we can use our childhood memories and imaginations to shape the places we live and love. (Recorded at Play@TED on May 14, 2026)

entry.title: Photographer Platon says empathy is the secret ingredient for finding a human connection. #TEDTalks

media:group.media:title: Photographer Platon says empathy is the secret ingredient for finding a human connection. #TEDTalks
media:group.media:description: With his art, photographer Platon seeks to strip away assumptions and leave viewers with a window into his subject's character, filling our eyes with wonder and curiosity. Sharing extraordinary stories of what it's like to photograph some of the world's most prominent figures -- from Michelle Obama and Pussy Riot to Vladimir Putin and Muhammad Ali -- Platon captures the disarming power of empathy and human connection.
